title: Diesel Fuel System Health and Safety Precautions
introduction:
I treat pressure release and engine cooling as separate prerequisites for fuel-system work. Meeting one does not satisfy the other: pressure and heat present different injury hazards.

The warning symbol marks the precaution below. This page explains the conditions that must be met before work begins; it does not provide a pressure-release method, a cooling interval or a procedure for confirming those conditions.

edits.text: WARNING: Do not begin work on the fuel system until the fuel-system pressure has been released and the engine has cooled. Fuel in the high-pressure fuel system is hot and under very high pressure. High-pressure fuel can cause cuts, and contact with hot fuel can cause burns. Failure to follow these instructions may result in serious personal injury.
edits.why: Cooling addresses the heat hazard; pressure release addresses the pressure hazard. Both prerequisites must be satisfied before fuel-system work begins.
